{{Quote|Before we begin, let's get something straight. I don't like hotshots. If you want to impress me, show me control and discipline. Without them you won't stand a chance against the Empire.|Jake Farrell|audio=Farrell1-RA.flac|<ref name="RA" />}}
'''Jake Farrell''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] who served in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] prior to the [[Declaration of a New Order]]. Following the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] at the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Farrell became an instructor for the Empire, but retired from Imperial service after a series of increasingly ruthless missions. He eventually came out of retirement and joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], teaching Rebel pilots the skills needed to fight against the Empire. Known as a top [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] pilot, Farrell flew a modified [[R-22 Spearhead starfighter|R-22 Spearhead]] during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. His experience with the R-22 led to him being selected to help design the new [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]], which was based on the R-22. When the first A-wings entered service, Farrell transferred to an A-wing [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]].

By the time of the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], he was considered to be among the best A-wing pilots, and so was chosen to fly with [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Green Squadron]] in the assault on the Imperial [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]]. Participating in the starfighter attack on the Death Star's [[Hypermatter reactor/Legends|main reactor]], Farrell followed the order of [[Gold Leader/Legends|Gold Leader]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] to break off his run and head for the surface of the [[Space station/Legends|station]], drawing off some of the Imperial [[TIE series/Legends|TIE fighters]] in pursuit.

==Biography==
===Early career===
In the years prior to the [[Declaration of a New Order|declaration]] of a [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], Jake Farrell, a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], served the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] as a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]].<ref name="RA manual" /> When the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] ended in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] transformed the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] with himself as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> and Farrell went on to serve the new [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], helping to train some of the best pilots in the Empire. However, as the Empire grew more ruthless, Farrell found himself sent on ever more destructive missions.<ref name="RA manual" /> Watching the pilots he had trained help to further Palpatine's subjugation of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|256|Farrell, Jake}}</ref> Farrell decided to retire, leaving the Imperial Navy and fleeing to a secret location to pass the rest of his life in peace.<ref name="RA manual" />

===Alliance instructor===
{{Quote|Well done, Rookie One. It looks like you've earned yourself an A-wing. But don't try any stunts with Commander Farrell. He won't appreciate it.|Merrick Simms to Rookie One|audio=Simms2-RA.flac|<ref name="RA" />}}
[[File:FarrellRA.png|thumb|left|220px|Jake Farrell, shortly before the Battle of Yavin]]
Years later,<ref name="CSWE" /> after the [[Corellian Treaty|rise]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> Farrell came out of retirement and joined the fledgling Rebellion as an instructor in the [[Alliance Starfighter Corps/Legends|Alliance Starfighter Corps]], in the hopes of providing young pilots with the skills they would need to fight the Empire.<ref name="RA manual" /> Farrell originally flew [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighters]] and was considered one of the Rebellion's top X-wing pilots.<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Green Squadron Pilot}}</ref> Despite this, Farrell preferred the extra speed and maneuverability of the [[R-22 Spearhead starfighter|R-22 Spearhead]] and spent much time upgrading the fighter to further improve its performance.<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="0BBY">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]'' takes place at the same time as the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places in 0 BBY.</ref> Farrell held the rank of [[Commander/Legends|commander]] and was using his experience to train rookie pilots. One of his trainees was "[[Rookie One]]," who was sent to Farrell after passing his piloting trials through [[Beggar's Canyon/Legends|Beggar's Canyon]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Flying a pair of R-22 Spearheads, Farrell led Rookie One through the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system's]] [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid field]], instructing him to dodge the rock asteroids and shoot any ice ones in his path. Impressed by Rookie One's performance, Farrell passed him and ordered the young pilot to report to [[Kolaador]] for the final phase of his training.<ref name="RA" />

Shortly after Rookie One's training, the Empire dispatched the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], a [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] which was capable of destroying a [[Planet/Legends|planet]], to destroy the [[Great Temple/Legends|Rebel base]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].<ref name="RA" /> Having managed to acquire the [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] to the [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]], [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] devised a plan to destroy it&mdash;a direct [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] hit on a small [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] would trigger a chain reaction in the battlestation's [[Reactor|main reactor]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Farrell took a pair of modified R-22 Spearheads to Yavin 4<ref name="TEGW" /> and flew one of the fighters in the subsequent [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Working alongside his former pupil, Rookie One, along with numerous other Alliance starfighter pilots, Farrell helped to fight the Imperial forces<ref name="Insider27">{{InsiderCite|27|LucasArts Update|Excerpts from the Journal of a Rebel Pilot}}</ref> until [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]] pilot [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] scored the decisive blow.<ref name="ANH" />

Following the Battle of Yavin, General Dodonna, [[Adar Tallon/Legends|Adar Tallon]] and [[Walex Blissex/Legends|Walex Blissex]] realized that the Alliance needed a faster starfighter than the X-wing to counter the latest Imperial [[TIE series/Legends|TIE models]]. The resulting starfighter, the [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]], was based on the R-22 Spearhead, and Farrell's experience modifying the fighters saw him recruited to help draw up the designs.<ref name="TEGW" /> When the new starfighters entered service, Farrell transferred to an A-wing unit.<ref name="CCG" />

===The Battle of Endor===
{{Quote|Split up and head back to the surface. And see if you can get a few of those TIE fighters to follow you.''"<br />"''Copy, Gold Leader.|Jake Farrell acknowledges Lando Calrissian's order to draw off Imperial pursuit|<ref name="ROTJ" />}}
[[File:Endorshaft.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Farrell and Wedge Antilles fly ahead of the ''Millennium Falcon'' into the second Death Star.]]
[[4 ABY/Legends|Four years later]],<ref name="NEC" /> the Alliance learned that the Empire had constructed a [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]], more powerful than the first.<ref name="ROTJ" /> When the time came for the Rebel Alliance to [[Battle of Endor/Legends|attack]] the new battlestation, Farrell, as one of the best A-wing operators, was chosen to fly with [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Green Squadron]]<ref name="CCG" /> with the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] [[Green Four/Legends|Green Four]].<ref name="TEGW" /> In the initial stages of the battle, Green Squadron and other A-wing units used their [[4x-Phantom Short-Range Sensor Jammer/Legends|jamming units]] to disrupt Imperial [[Targeting computer/Legends|targeting computers]].<ref name="GG5">[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi'', Second Edition]]</ref> As the battle progressed, Green Squadron pilots scored many kills on Imperial fighters<ref name="FF">{{FactFile|13|AWI 1-2|A-Wing Starfighter}}</ref> and Farrell joined [[Green Leader/Legends|Green Leader]] [[Arvel Crynyd/Legends|Arvel Crynyd]] to bring down the [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] protecting the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] of the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], leading to the destruction of the Imperial [[Command ship/Legends|command ship]].<ref name="TEGW" />

Following the Alliance battle plan, once the deflector shield around the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] was deactivated by [[Endor strike team/Legends|Rebel operatives]], the leader of the starfighter assault, [[Gold Leader/Legends|Gold Leader]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], called for fighters to follow him into the battlestation's superstructure for a strike on the Death Star's [[Hypermatter reactor/Legends|main reactor]]. Farrell, among a group of others including [[Red Leader/Legends|Red Leader]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]],<ref name="ROTJ" /> [[Gray Leader/Legends|Gray Leader]] [[Horton Salm/Legends|Horton Salm]],<ref name="RS">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref> [[Green Three/Legends|Green Three]] [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]],<ref name="CCG-3">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Green Squadron 3}}</ref> and [[Red Seven/Legends|Red Seven]] [[Keir Santage/Legends|Keir Santage]],<ref name="DSII-Santage">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Keir Santage}}</ref> complied, diving into the workings of the partially-completed [[Space station/Legends|station]].<ref name="ROTJ" /> Following Antilles' X-wing, Farrell flew ahead of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], which was followed by Celchu's A-wing, Salm's [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing]], and Santage's X-wing.<ref name="MS">{{WebCite|url=http://www.michaelastackpole.com/?page_id=33|text=Frequently Asked Questions|author=[[Michael A. Stackpole]]|date=2010-03-02|work=Stormwolf.com|archivedate=20170627124751}}</ref><ref name="ROTJ" />

Imperial fighters&mdash;three [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighters]] and three [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE Interceptors]]&mdash;chased the Rebel fighters as they flew through the Death Star, posing a threat to the success of the mission. One of the Imperial [[Starship/Legends|ships]] was destroyed when it collided with a wall, but, after Santage's X-wing was shot down, Calrissian ordered a number of the Alliance fighters to split up and head back to the surface, in order to draw off some of the Imperial pursuit.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Farrell was the first to comply, followed by Celchu and Salm&mdash;he and the others who broke off managed to draw off two Imperial fighters, reducing Calrissian's remaining pursuit by half.<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> Farrell survived the battle<ref name="TLC" /> and, due in part to his success in lessening the number of pursuers, Calrissian and Antilles were able to complete their mission of torpedoing the reactor, destroying the Death Star and winning the battle for the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Afterwards, he celebrated the end of the Empire.<ref name="TLC" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|You impressed Commander Farrell. That's not easy.|Ru Murleen|audio=Murleen2-RA.flac|<ref name="RA" />}}
[[File:JakeFarrell-TLC.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Jake Farrell, around the time of the Battle of Endor]]
Farrell was a serious officer with a no-nonsense attitude<ref name="RA manual" /> and little time for pilots who showed off during training.<ref name="RA" /> Though he could seem grumpy, this was largely a way of teaching control and discipline to his students,<ref name="CSWE" /> qualities that he believed were vital if Alliance pilots were to defeat their Imperial opponents. Only those that demonstrated these skills would impress the commander and pass his training.<ref name="RA" />

Farrell favored the speed and maneuverability of the R-22 Spearhead and modified his own fighter to improve its performance by upgrading its systems and removing any non-essential components. Farrells skills saw him brought into General Dodonna's team to work on the design of the RZ-1 A-wing interceptor.<ref name="TEGW" /> Already considered among the top X-wing pilots in the Rebel Alliance before the introduction of the A-wing, Farrell transferred to an A-wing unit when the new craft became available. By the time of the Battle of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], he was already considered to be one of the best A-wing pilots as well, and so was chosen to fly in Green Squadron<ref name="CCG" /> alongside such notables as Arvel Crynyd<ref name="ROTJ" /> and Tycho Celchu.<ref name="CCG-3" /> When Calrissian asked for fighters to join him in his assault on the Death Star's reactor, Farrel was among the first to answer the call; when the general gave the order for a number of fighters to break off the assault on the Death Star's main reactor in order to draw off pursuit, he complied, allowing his fellow pilots to complete the mission,<ref name="ROTJ" /> for which they received accolade.<ref name="RS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Hey, don't you know you shouldn't be flying up here alone?|Jake Farrell to Rookie One during the Battle of Yavin|audio=Farrell2-RA.flac|<ref name="RA" />}}
The character of Jake Farrell was created for the [[1993]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]'' and his backstory was expanded in the game's manual.<ref name="RA manual" /><ref name="RA" /> In making ''Rebel Assault'', the developers used characters and scenes from the ''[[The Star Wars Trilogy]]'' as a basis for those in the game.<ref name="Insider's Guide">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault: The Official Insider's Guide]]''</ref> Farrell's appearance was based on a pilot played by actor [[Michael Drew]]<ref name="MD1">{{WebCite|url=http://www.kractors.co.nz/detailsx.php?act_id=373|text=Michael Drew Details|work=[https://www.kractors.co.nz/ KRA]|archivedate=20180130203414}}</ref><ref name="MD2">{{WebCite|url=http://jedibusiness.com/figureDetails.aspx?id=266|text=Jake Farrell Figure, Rebel Pilot Legacy III, Star Wars The Legacy Collection|work=jedibusiness.com|archivedate=20150320085829}}</ref><ref name="MD3">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsautographcollection.com/content/imperial-signings-wing-pilot-michael-drew|text=Imperial Signings: A-wing Pilot Michael Drew|work=starwarsautographcollection.com|archivedate=20170331141031}}</ref> who can be seen briefly in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], in which he acknowledges Lando Calrissian's order for the Rebel fighters to split up in order to draw off Imperial pursuers during the Death Star assault.<ref name="ROTJ" /> [[Decipher]] also fleshed out the character's backstory, with the release of the "''[[Death Star II Limited]]''" set for the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] in [[2000]], which established him as a top A-wing and former top X-wing pilot.<ref name="CCG" /> ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' ([[2012]]) further expanded the character's history, describing his part in the development of the RZ-1 A-wing interceptor.<ref name="TEGW" />

===Battle of Yavin===
[[File:FarrellYavin.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Farrell rescues Rookie One during the Battle of Yavin.]]
In ''Rebel Assault''{{'s}} final level, set during the Battle of Yavin, [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Blue Squadron]] attempt to destroy the Death Star by undertaking a trench run which contradicts the events depicted in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. The trench run in the game is almost identical to that of the movie&mdash;only the persons involved are different. In the game, [[Merrick Simms]] enters the trench first while [[Ru Murleen]] joins Rookie One and [[Thurlow Harris]] in providing cover. As they negotiate down the long trench the group is pursued by three TIE fighters, including a [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]] which was presumably intended to be the one used by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] in the movie. The TIEs open fire, killing Harris and forcing Murleen to pull out, echoing the fates of [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]] and Wedge Antilles in the movie. Simms finally reaches firing range but his torpedoes impact on the surface, leaving Rookie One next to make an attempt. With the TIEs closing fast, Rookie One appears to be in trouble when Farrell's R-22 arrives and destroys the TIEs, leaving Rookie One free to take his shot. This again parallels [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] last minute rescue of Luke Skywalker from the film. Finally, it is Rookie One's shot that is depicted as destroying the battlestation, as opposed to Skywalker's.<ref name="RA" /><ref name="ANH" />

In December [[2006]] [[Leland Chee]] commented on the [[StarWars.com]] [[StarWars.com Message Boards|Message Boards]] that Rookie One's trench run was non-[[canon]].<ref>{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=1062#16021160|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-12-07|time=6:15 PM}}</ref> ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' later confirmed that Blue Squadron were assigned to attack the Death Star's [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] while Red and [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold]] Squadrons attacked the trench.<ref name="TEGW" /> Although [[Sue Seserman]]'s [[Star Wars Insider 27|''Star Wars Insider'' 27]] article "[[LucasArts Update|''Excerpts from the Journal of a Rebel Pilot'']]" confirms that Farrell was present with Murleen and Rookie One for the Battle of Yavin, since his only appearance during the battle in the game is during the non-canon trench run, the exact nature of his involvement in the battle is unclear.<ref name="RA" /> "''Excerpts from the Journal of a Rebel Pilot''" incorrectly refers to the character as [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] Ferrell.<ref name="Insider27" />

===Inconsistencies===
{{Quote|Red Two, peel off and take the rest of the assault wing back to the surface. Try to get those TIE fighters and make them follow you out.''"<br />"''Copy, Gold Leader.|Lando Calrissian and Red Two, who serves in Farrell's role in the ''Return of the Jedi'' radio drama|<ref name="ROTJ radio drama">{{RJRadio|Blood of a Jedi}}</ref>}}
Farrell's role in the Battle of Endor has been depicted by a number of adaptations of the movie without change;<ref name="SWM">[[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi 4|''Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi'' 4]]</ref><ref name="JN">[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]]</ref><ref name="PC">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi Cine-Manga|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' Cine-Manga]]</ref> however, in some versions, his line is given to other characters. In the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] of ''Return of the Jedi'', Farrell does not appear, and his role is instead assumed by Green Leader&mdash;Arvel Crynyd&mdash;who follows Calrissian into the Death Star.<ref name="ROTJ novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref>

The [[Return of the Jedi (radio)|''Return of the Jedi'' audio drama]] and ''[[Return of the Jedi: The National Public Radio Dramatization]]'' script combine the roles of Farrell and that of [[Red Two (Battle of Endor)|Red Two]], a Y-wing pilot seen in the film. In the radio drama, Red Two follows Calrissian into the Death Star and responds to a command to head back to the surface in order to draw TIE fighters away.<ref name="ROTJ radio drama" /><ref name="NPR">[[Return of the Jedi: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''Return of the Jedi'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref>

===Fan misconception===
For a time there was fan speculation as to the identity of the pilot who appears in ''Return of the Jedi'', as author [[Michael A. Stackpole]] had established Tycho Celchu as an A-wing pilot who survived the Death Star run in the Battle of Endor in his [[1996]] novel ''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''. However, Stackpole confirmed on his website that Farrell (then-unnamed) is not Celchu, stating that Celchu does not look like Farrell, and that while Farrell flew the first A-wing into the Death Star, Celchu piloted the second.<ref name="MS" /> Furthermore, other cards released by Decipher for the card game indicate Celchu as the pilot of the second A-wing in the chase sequence<ref name="CCG-3" /> and as one of the background characters during the Alliance briefing before the battle, who does not look like Farrell.<ref name="CCG-C">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Tycho Celchu}}</ref>
